title: Interactive geographic briefing
question: Can an AI agent build a slide briefing with one map slide per area and context from another layer?
answer: Yes, in an open GISMap page. The agent loads the primary layer, builds a briefing-v1 document (one slide per selected feature, each with its camera, highlighted selection, narrative and contextual layers), validates it, and shares one link that opens as a desktop deck or a mobile swipe feed.
triggers: Build an interactive crime briefing for Philadelphia
Make a presentation with one slide per county

required.name: primaryLayer
required.description: The layer whose features become slides.

required.name: selection
required.description: Feature IDs, a filter, or 'all', plus the slide order.

optional.name: contextLayer
optional.description: A second layer shown and related per slide (spatialRel, distance).

optional.name: narrative
optional.description: Titles and text grounded in inspected data.

optional.name: template
optional.description: filter-series, timeline, grid-atlas or spatial-3d-chart for data-driven slides.

steps.action: Read llms.txt, this recipe and api/capabilities.json; note the engine and execution environment you actually have.
Read the source metadata: geometry type, field names and types, spatial reference, extent, sentinels and query support. Query real values before filtering; never invent fields.
Pick stable feature IDs and the slide order. For context layers, decide the spatial relationship; an overlay alone is not evidence that points fall inside a polygon.
Validate the document statically before loading it.
Load or generate the briefing in the open page. Slide layers with a relation query the context layer's service per slide, so counts come from the service, not from the drawing.
Step through every slide on desktop and in a narrow (mobile) viewport: selected feature, highlight, camera, context layer, narrative numbers. State whether counts are complete, filtered or sampled.
Create the link, then reopen it. Optional PDF handout and QR card.

artifact.structure: A briefing-v1 document: layerId, selection, ordered slides (template, camera, blocks, layers with relations, optional dataView/timeline/spatialChart), shared with the map's layers, styles and skin.

outputs.format: Desktop deck and mobile swipe feed
outputs.notes: The same document; the layout follows the screen.

verification: Each slide frames and highlights the intended feature
Context layer loaded and related by a real spatial query
The shared link reopens to the same slides
limitations: Briefings need the in-page API; there is no hosted authoring endpoint.
Links hold at most 60 slides and must fit the URL budget; large documents use ?briefing=<hosted JSON>.
Data-driven templates sample at most 500 features (generateTemplate coverage is 'unknown').
recovery: If a relation query fails, the slide notes it; show both layers and say the analysis is incomplete.
If the link is too long, host the JSON and use ?briefing=<URL>, or export a .gmo project.

examples.title: Philadelphia police divisions and districts
examples.prompt: Build a briefing with one slide per Philadelphia police division showing the districts inside it.

dataset.label: Philadelphia Police Divisions and Districts (City of Philadelphia)

checks: Opened headless: both layers loaded and the deck started at slide 1 of 9.
Per-slide highlight, mobile swipe and PDF were not rechecked in this pass.
